Rábida's red sand is visible even from the boat. Iron in the volcanic rocks gives the shore a rich rust-colored hue, especially striking against the blue water. After landing, it is pleasant to walk along the surf and watch the wet sand darken as the waves leave trails of white foam.

Sea lions rest on the shore, while brown pelicans nest in the shrubs behind the beach. Farther inland lies a saltwater lagoon where waterbirds feed. Flamingos also occur here, although their presence varies. Every wildlife encounter is different: one visit may be remembered for birds at the water's edge, another for sea lions moving across the beach.

Rábida lies south of Santiago and makes a rewarding stop on a cruise through the islands of the archipelago. A short walk along its shore is enough to see the animals and the unusual color of the volcanic earth. Photographers will especially enjoy the contrast between red sand, dry hillsides and the ocean, even on an ordinary sunny day.

The ascent to Rano Kau is part of excursions to the ceremonial village of Orongo. From the crater rim, visitors can see the lake and vegetation within the volcanic basin. This natural landscape adds another dimension to the island's archaeological sites.

Rano Raraku is on Easter Island, Rapa Nui. The slopes of this extinct volcano were once a quarry where most of the moai were carved. Many of the figures remain here: some stand on the hillsides, while others lie among rocks and grass.

Walking through the site helps visitors imagine how the stone statues were made. The moai are scattered across different parts of the slope, giving the quarry a very different appearance from ceremonial platforms with restored rows of figures.

Rano Raraku is included in excursions along the island's southern coast together with Ahu Tongariki. After visiting the archaeological sites, the route may continue to Anakena Beach.

Raqchi is an archaeological complex in the Vilcanota Valley south of Cusco. Its main attraction is the Temple of Viracocha, with a tall central wall combining a stone base and an upper section of adobe. The remains of columns help visitors picture the structure of the large roofed building.

Circular storehouses and other buildings from the Inca settlement also survive on the site. A walk through the complex reveals both the temple architecture and the organization of the surrounding space. Raqchi lies on the cultural route between Cusco and Puno.

The river section of the approach to Angel Falls ends at Ratoncito Island. From here, a trail leads through tropical vegetation past streams, large trees, orchids, bromeliads and moss-covered rocks.

On the one-day excursion, the stop at Ratoncito comes before an approximately one-hour walk to Laime. Views of the waterfall plunging from the high cliffs already open up at this stage.
